dia-de-muertos-en-mixquic.titulo_en: Day of the Dead in Mixquic
dia-de-muertos-en-mixquic.descripcion_en: The magical neighborhood of Mixquic welcomes the faithful departed with its traditional offerings full of food, drinks and personal belongings of the deceased, in the ritual known as "La Alumbrada." Every home is filled with the scent of cempasúchil (marigold) flowers, fruit, copal incense and candles. You will experience this ancient, 100% Mexican tradition, where devotion and customs surrounding death come together to create an experience unlike any other in the world.

With spectacular landscapes, unique viewpoints and a railway that crosses the sierra and mountains, it is one of Mexico's must-see destinations.

Overnight in Chihuahua.

08:30 am meeting in the hotel lobby for a land transfer to Creel, a Magical Town (Pueblo Mágico). Along the way we will visit the Mennonite Community in Cuauhtémoc (closed on Sundays). You can visit the different viewpoints, take the cable car and ziplines (optional, not included), Piedra Volada and the suspension bridge. Optional tasting of the typical Divisadero gorditas. itinerario_en.descripcion_en: We begin at the El Tule Tree with its impressive canopy and height, then head to Teotitlán del Valle to learn about natural dyeing, admire the ancient fretwork of Mitla, walk before the waterfalls of Hierve el Agua, and finish by enjoying an artisanal mezcal.

itinerario_en.titulo_en: Oaxaca – Monte Albán – Alebrijes and Black Clay
itinerario_en.descripcion_en: It begins at Monte Albán, the ancient Zapotec capital, walking among temples and terraces. It continues to Arrazola, where alebrijes come to life in an authentic workshop: carving, painting, and traditional techniques with no mandatory purchases. It ends in San Bartolo Coyotepec, famous for its black clay pottery.

A half-day walking tour through downtown Oaxaca: the main square, the cathedral, the Santo Domingo church, and its colorful streets. The rest of the afternoon is free for shopping, museums, or sampling mezcal.
Transfer to Oaxaca airport. End of services.

itinerario_en.titulo_en: San Cristóbal – Agua Azul, Misol-Ha and Palenque
itinerario_en.descripcion_en: Early departure toward Palenque. Stop in Ocosingo for breakfast. Visit to the Agua Azul Waterfalls Park, formed by the confluence of the Otulún, Shumuljá, and Tulijá rivers. Continue to the Misol-Ha Waterfall (40 m high). Guided tour of the Palenque Archaeological Zone, one of the most important Mayan sites in Mesoamerica. Return to San Cristóbal.

itinerario_en.titulo_en: San Cristóbal – El Chiflón Waterfalls – Montebello Lakes
itinerario_en.descripcion_en: Visit to the El Chiflón Waterfalls, a chain of waterfalls formed by the San Vicente River (El Suspiro, Ala de Ángel, Arco Iris, Quinceañera, and the main one, Velo de Novia, at 120 m). Continue to the Montebello Lakes, where we will visit Tziscao and the international lake on the border with Guatemala. Return to San Cristóbal.

itinerario_en.descripcion_en: Visit to the lookout points of the Sumidero Canyon. A 1 hour 50 minute boat ride on the Grijalva River: the Chicoasén dam, the Virgin's cave, and the Christmas tree rock formation. Free time in the magical town of Chiapa de Corzo. Return to San Cristóbal.
Free morning and, at the agreed time, transfer to Tuxtla Gutiérrez airport. End of services.

itinerario_en.descripcion_en: The Don Vasco Route is a cultural and sightseeing tour through Michoacán following in the footsteps of the missionary Vasco de Quiroga, visiting Pátzcuaro, Tzintzuntzan, and Quiroga. Return to Morelia.
After breakfast, departure toward Querétaro. In the afternoon, a trolley tour to explore the city. Overnight in Querétaro.
Departure toward the wine route, visiting the magical towns of Tequisquiapan and San Sebastián de Bernal. Cheese tasting and a visit to one of the oldest vineyards on the route. Return to Querétaro.
Transfer to Guanajuato. In the afternoon, a walking tour through streets and alleyways. In the evening, an activity with a traditional student minstrel group (estudiantina). Overnight in Guanajuato.
Visit to Dolores Hidalgo, cradle of Independence, the Atotonilco sanctuary, and San Miguel de Allende, with its Parish of San Miguel Arcángel. Return to Guanajuato.

Guided tour of Guanajuato: the Mummies Museum, the El Pípila Monument, the tunnels, the mine in the Valenciana neighborhood, the Church of San Cayetano, and the local market. 16:00 hrs transfer to Guadalajara (airport or hotel). End of services.

tour-tequila-tradicion-con-distincion.descripcion_en: Enjoy a tour designed for those seeking memorable experiences, luxury transportation, fine cuisine, personalized service, and access to authentic tequila culture. We welcome you with a cantarito in hand; learn about the care and cultivation of the agave plant, visit the distillery where experts will walk you through the distillation process, and finish with a guided tasting of three of our expressions: blanco, reposado, and añejo tequila.

They will be your guides in a clay modeling practice that will allow you to appreciate the effort put into each handicraft, which you will be able to take home. Afterward, enjoy free time in this lovely town to try the local cuisine, buy souvenirs and handicrafts, or simply wander its picturesque streets.

isla-de-mezcala-y-ajijic.descripcion_en: Isla de Mezcala, also known as Isla del Presidio, is located across from the town of Mezcala de la Asunción. This place was used as a strategic point by the army as a defensive fort against the Spanish government. Later, El Presidio operated from 1826 to 1855 for the towns near Lake Chapala in Jalisco and Michoacán, where most of the criminals arrived at the Presidio de Mezcala accused of crimes of violation. At the end of the tour we continue our visit with a stop for lunch in Ajijic, a magical town that charms visitors with its simplicity, its boardwalk and its colorful streets.

senderismo-petroglifos-mezcala.titulo_en: Hiking and Petroglyphs at Isla de Mezcala
senderismo-petroglifos-mezcala.descripcion_en: The petroglyphs of Isla de Mezcala are pre-Hispanic carvings etched in rock by the ancient inhabitants of the Lake Chapala region. These designs include geometric figures, human representations and symbolic elements that reflect aspects of their worldview. They are an important testimony to the archaeological heritage of Jalisco and contribute to the knowledge of the cultures that inhabited the region before the arrival of the Spanish. To finish, we will make a brief stop for lunch in the town of Ajijic, a magical town that charms visitors with its simplicity and its colorful streets.
